curation.lead:
An archived November 6, 2018 biography from Paul Weiss listed SoftBank among Brad Karp’s recent clients in significant securities, commercial, and regulatory matters [Finding #13162]. The firm page establishes prior SoftBank work but does not identify its matter, scope, billing client, or Rajeev Misra as Karp’s personal client [Finding #13162].

On January 26, 2019, Jeffrey Epstein asked Karp whether he represented Misra, and Karp first replied, “Sort of” [EFTA02627034][Finding #13074]. He then wrote, “Spoke to him yesterday” [EFTA02627034][Finding #13074]. Twelve minutes later Epstein told Reid Weingarten, “brad represent softbank, not rajeev, but did speak to him yesterday, re DB” [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028577][Finding #13163]. The categorical SoftBank/not-Misra wording and “re DB” were Epstein’s relay, not Karp’s words, and the record does not independently identify the conversation’s subject or a personal Misra engagement [Finding #13163].

Weingarten separately discussed possibly using Ron Soffer for what he called the “Softbank caper” and asked Epstein not to mention his role to Karp until they considered it useful [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028576][HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028577][Finding #13272][Finding #13074]. Those messages do not state that Weingarten or Soffer was retained and do not establish a common mandate [Finding #13272][Finding #13074]. In a separate FTX multidistrict-litigation matter, Karp’s appearance names four Temasek-related defendants and does not name the SoftBank entities that are other parties in the litigation [Finding #13249].

sections.title: Karp and Misra in the January 2019 Record
sections.content:
An archived November 6, 2018 biography from Paul Weiss listed SoftBank among Brad Karp's recent clients in significant securities, commercial, and regulatory matters [Finding #13162]. The firm page establishes prior SoftBank work but does not identify its matter, scope, billing client, or Rajeev Misra as Karp's personal client [Finding #13162].

On January 26, 2019, Jeffrey Epstein asked Karp, “Rajeev misra do you represent?” and Karp first replied, “Sort of” [EFTA02627034][Finding #13074]. He then wrote, “Spoke to him yesterday” [EFTA02627034][Finding #13074]. Twelve minutes later, Epstein told Reid Weingarten, “brad represent softbank, not rajeev, but did speak to him yesterday, re DB” [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028577][Finding #13163]. The categorical SoftBank/not-Misra wording and “re DB” were Epstein's relay, not Karp's words; the record does not independently identify “DB,” the conversation's subject, or a personal Misra engagement [Finding #13163].

Weingarten separately discussed possibly using Ron Soffer on what he called the “Softbank caper” and asked Epstein not to mention his role to Karp until they considered it useful [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028576][HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028577][Finding #13272][Finding #13074]. Those messages do not state that Weingarten or Soffer was retained and do not show that Karp knew of their discussion or joined a common mandate [Finding #13272][Finding #13074]. In a separate FTX multidistrict-litigation matter, Karp's appearance names four Temasek-related defendants and does not name the SoftBank entities that are other parties in the litigation [Finding #13249].

curation.system_role: The retained record distinguishes documented firm-level SoftBank work from unproven personal representation of Misra and from Karp’s separate Temasek appearance. It also separates Karp’s exact reply from Epstein’s stronger relay.
open_questions: What matter, dates, scope, and billing client underlay the archived Paul Weiss listing of SoftBank among Karp's recent clients [Finding #13162]?
What engagement, conflicts, billing, or calendar records identify the subject and status of Karp's January 25, 2019 conversation with Misra [Finding #13074]?

What did Epstein mean by ‘DB’ in his January 26 relay, and what source beyond Epstein's message supports or contradicts the SoftBank/not-Misra characterization [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028577][Finding #13163]?
Did Weingarten or Ron Soffer open a matter, perform work, or bill Misra after the January 25–26 discussion [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028576][Finding #13272]?
Which lawyers represented the SoftBank entities named elsewhere in the FTX MDL, and were their matters related to the Temasek defendants represented by Karp [Finding #13249]?

citation_findings.summary: An archived November 6, 2018 Paul, Weiss biography listed SoftBank among Karp’s recent clients in significant securities, commercial, and regulatory matters.
citation_findings.detail: This official archived firm biography independently establishes that Karp had represented SoftBank by November 6, 2018. It does not identify the matter, dates, scope, billing client, or Rajeev Misra as Karp’s client, and it does not establish that the January 2019 Misra conversation concerned an existing SoftBank engagement.

citation_findings.summary: Document metadata places Epstein’s receipt of Karp’s ambiguous Misra reply at 1:00 p.m. EST on January 26, 2019; Epstein relayed a stronger characterization to Reid Weingarten at 1:12 p.m., twelve minutes later.
citation_findings.detail: Karp answered “Sort of. Spoke to him yesterday” when asked whether he represented Rajeev Misra. Twelve minutes after the source document’s date-received timestamp (1548525600 = 18:00 UTC = 1:00 p.m. EST), Epstein told Weingarten “brad represent softbank, not rajeev, but did speak to him yesterday, re DB.” The categorical SoftBank/not-Misra formulation and “re DB” appear in Epstein’s relay, not in Karp’s written reply; they therefore cannot be treated as Karp’s exact words or as independent proof of the engagement or call subject. “DB” remains unresolved.

citation_findings.summary: A January 2025 CourtListener docket entry personally names Karp for four Temasek-related defendants in the FTX multidistrict litigation; SoftBank entities appear elsewhere in the MDL party list, but the Karp entry does not name them as his clients.
citation_findings.detail: Docket entry 809 adds Karp for Artz Fund Investments Private Limited, Blakiston Investments Pte. Ltd., Temasek International (USA) LLC, and Temasek International Private Limited. The broader MDL metadata includes SoftBank II Tempest (DE) LLC, SoftBank Investment Advisers (UK) Limited, SoftBank Group Corp., and SoftBank Global Advisers Limited as other parties. The record therefore supports a personal Karp-to-Temasek legal edge, not a Karp-to-SoftBank edge.

citation_findings.summary: January 25-26, 2019 messages separately document Weingarten asking Epstein for insights while considering representation of Misra and considering Ron Soffer for what Weingarten called the Softbank caper; the messages do not establish that Weingarten or Soffer was retained.
citation_findings.detail: On January 25, Weingarten asked Epstein for special insights about Rajeev Misra, and Epstein answered conditionally, If he wants you to rep him. YES. On January 26, in a separate exchange about Ron Soffer, Weingarten wrote that he was thinking about using him on the Softbank caper; Epstein replied go slow, and Weingarten then asked Epstein to get the book on Soffer. The same thread later records Epstein relaying a Karp/SoftBank representation claim and Weingarten asking that his role not be mentioned to Karp. These messages document prospective-client and lawyer-vetting discussions, not a proved retention or common mandate.
